identity.note: UFC athlete page: Valentina Shevchenko, women's flyweight, Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, age 38. Boxing records match by name, Kyrgyz nationality, Peru-based bouts 2010-2011; the 2007 Russian women's boxing bracket also lists sister Antonina Shevchenko at 60 kg, consistent with identity.

wrestling.note: UFC page says she trained wrestling under coach Pavel Fedotov; no competitive wrestling record found. Wikipedia mentions only a 2013 TV exhibition, not a credential. UWW database not searched.

grappling.note: No submission-grappling results found in the sources read; ADCC records not searched.

claims.text: A 2002 Kyrgyz news report lists her among the successful girls at the national youth judo championship in Tokmak, without stating her placing or weight class.
Sherdog lists judo among five disciplines in which she holds the Master of Sport designation; no event or year is given.
claims.level_note: Master of Sport rank, self-reported style biography claim

judo.note: Wikipedia's 2002 Kyrgyz national judo title at 58 kg is not supported by its own cited source: that article (msn.kg, Dec 2002) covers a national youth (18 and under) championship in Tokmak and only says she succeeded in her weight class, with no placing or weight given. Black belt claim rests on MMA

claims.text: IFMA credits her with seven Muay Thai world championship titles: 2003, 2006, 2007, 2008 (57 kg), 2009 and 2012 (60 kg), and 2010 (63.5 kg).
IFMA lists her as Muay Thai gold medallist at 60 kg at the SportAccord World Combat Games in 2010 (China) and 2013 (Russia).
IFMA lists her as 2010 Pan American champion and 2011 South American champion in Muay Thai at 60 kg.
A Kyrgyz news report says she won the women's sparring event at the first Kyrgyzstan kickboxing championship in Sokuluk in 2002.
24.kg reported that she won gold at the 2007 Russian Thai boxing championship in Yekaterinburg, competing as a Kyrgyz athlete.
claims.level_note: Russian national Muay Thai championship won as a foreign (Kyrgyz) entrant

claims.text: Wikipedia credits her with a 2003 WAKO world kickboxing bronze and a 2004 WAKO world title in Italy at 56 kg; no WAKO record could be opened to confirm either.

kickboxing.note: Verified via Muay Thai (IFMA, the sport's world governing body); Muay Thai has no separate discipline slot here. WAKO 2003 bronze and 2004 world title remain unverified: Wikipedia's cited WAKO results page returns 404 and the Tapology bout page could not be opened; a search for a 2004 WAKO event in

claims.text: At the 2007 Russian women's national amateur boxing championships in Odintsovo she reached the 57 kg final and lost it on points to Elena Gorshkova, finishing runner-up.
She boxed professionally twice in Peru and won both: a 10-round decision over Halanna dos Santos in May 2010 and a stoppage of Nurys Rincon in December 2011.
WomenBoxing.com records her pro boxing record as 2-0, with wins in Callao in 2010 and Lima in 2011.

sources_checked.name: Amateur Boxing Results (strefa.pl), 9th Russian Women's Championships 2007

boxing.note: Conflict resolved against Wikipedia: Wikipedia calls her 2007 Russian women's national amateur champion at 57 kg, but its own cited source (amateur-boxing.strefa.pl, based on Russian Boxing Federation data) shows she reached the 57 kg final and lost it 23:5 to Elena Gorshkova. Pro record 2-0 confirm
